chunks: Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazi' narrated from Hamzah ibn Zayd, from 'Ali ibn Suwayd, from Abu al-Hasan Musa عليه السلام, who said:

When our Qa'im عليه السلام rises, he will say: ‘O company of horsemen, travel in the middle of the road; O company of pedestrians, travel along the sides of the road. So whichever horseman takes to the sides of the road and injures a man, we shall impose the blood-money upon him; and whichever man takes to the middle of the road and is injured, then there is no blood-money for him.’

key_terms.الدِّيَةَ: financial compensation owed for bodily injury
key_terms.الْفُرْسَانِ: horsemen or mounted riders using the roadway
key_terms.جَنْبَيِ الطَّرِيقِ: the two sides of the road designated for pedestrians in this ruling
key_terms.عَيْبٌ: an injury or bodily harm inflicted upon a person
key_terms.قَائِمُنَا: the Qa'im of Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام who will arise with just rule
key_terms.وَسَطِ الطَّرِيقِ: the middle part of the road designated for mounted traffic in this ruling

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith say about liability when riders or pedestrians cause injury on the road under the rule of the Qa'im عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith sets out a legal ruling concerning liability for injury on the roadway, assigning different responsibilities to riders and pedestrians according to where each is supposed to travel. It also portrays the just governance of the Qa'im عليه السلام in regulating public order and protecting rights through clear legal standards.
